identity.name: Speedmaster Professional Moonwatch
identity.one_liner: The hand-wound, hesalite-crystal Moonwatch Omega sold with only minor changes for 24 years before replacing it with the co-axial caliber 3861 in 2021.

provenance_events.description: Buzz Aldrin wears his Omega Speedmaster Professional on the lunar surface during Apollo 11. NASA's qualification of the Speedmaster in 1965, after testing by astronaut candidates in a Houston simulation, makes it the first watch worn on the Moon.

narrative.story: Caliber 1861 replaced the 861 in the Speedmaster Professional line in 1997, a finishing and reliability update to a movement architecture that traces back to the manually wound caliber 321 NASA qualified for Apollo. Omega kept the 1861 essentially unchanged through reference 311.30.42.30.01.005, the hesalite-crystal Moonwatch, for 24 years — the longest run of any Speedmaster movement — before introducing the co-axial-escapement caliber 3861 in 2021 and phasing the 1861 out of the catalog.
narrative.collector_notes: Check dial print generation and hand luminova color against known transitional periods, whether the caseback is the closed steel Seahorse medallion (hesalite version) or a sapphire display back (a different, later reference), and service history — manual-wind chronographs see more winding-crown and pusher wear than automatics.
